<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **143** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fa26308bb0332152a359335be27ba1a7f18574de` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2cdd13a90259cbbaa61cce133bbd169e02a24ee3` — the merge of head `9fcf38b94b7c63e6e735dc3999d60a4710d5ccdf` into base `fa26308bb0332152a359335be27ba1a7f18574de`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2cdd13a90259cbbaa61cce133bbd169e02a24ee3 && git checkout 2cdd13a90259cbbaa61cce133bbd169e02a24ee3
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin fa26308bb0332152a359335be27ba1a7f18574de 9fcf38b94b7c63e6e735dc3999d60a4710d5ccdf && git checkout -B drift-repro fa26308bb0332152a359335be27ba1a7f18574de && git merge --no-ff 9fcf38b94b7c63e6e735dc3999d60a4710d5ccdf

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fa26308bb0332152a359335be27ba1a7f18574de
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs fa26308bb0332152a359335be27ba1a7f18574de` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Read-only throughout: files at the head and at origin/main through git show and git grep on a fetched ref; nothing built, run or re-run. The remainder of the diff (the changeset, the three content/docs/references pages, the generated en bundle) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT.

Check-runs on the head: 41, all completed. 36 success, 5 skipped by design (Console Pin Gate, Temporal Conformance, Dogfood Verify CLI, the dogfood matrix shard, Packed-tarball smoke). The five required contexts are success: Lint and Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard. No failure, nothing in progress. Head repo equals base repo; no governed path; 51 changed lines.

### ① Derived judgments

Each line the diff moves, judged against the rule the card quotes (cloud#3002 letter A: made here, not from a package, reads "authored in this system"; the system the caller is in drops the noun or says "this system"; a deployment or configuration scope keeps its word) and against the house spelling PR #24407 and PR #24413 landed.

1. `security/permission-set-owner-binding.ts:127`, the save, restore and publish `message` for an absent binding, now "authored in this system". RIGHT. The sense is "made here, not from a package"; #24413 and #24360 spell the same class "authored in this system". The refusal's `declared`, `bound`, `issueMessage` and the door set are untouched (read at the head, lines 94 to 150); the console at the pin parses none of the sentence. No accept set moves.
2. `security/permission.form.ts:52`, the `packageId` help text, "Leave empty for a set authored in this system." RIGHT, the same arm. Field, type and colSpan unchanged; the en bundle line 2337 is regenerated from it and matches it byte for byte.
3. `security/permission.zod.ts:680`, the `managedBy` tombstone prescription, "a set authored in this system carries neither". RIGHT. `retiredKey()` still refuses the key; the pin in `permission-set-managed-by-retirement.test.ts:57` is a regex whose `.*` spans the changed clause (nothing ever read the authored key `.*` Delete the key; a set's provenance is the package that ships it `.*` Run os migrate meta), so it holds without an edit, and Test Core is green on it.
4. `migrations/entries/semantic/18.permission-set-managed-by-retired.ts:18`, the upgrade-guide `replacement`, the same sentence as the tombstone. RIGHT. The entry's `id`, `surface`, `reason` and `acceptanceCriteria` are untouched; the registry projection gates (check:spec-changes and check:upgrade-guide, inside Lint and Repo Gates) are green. The tombstone and the entry still read identically, as before.
5. `system/auth-config.zod.ts:345`, `:401`, `:581`, TSDoc: "an app built on this system" and "this system's apps". RIGHT. `:401` and `:581` are the sentence PR #24407 gave the Setup Authentication group in `auth.manifest.ts`, so the spec's reference text and the console's help now read the same.
6. `system/auth-config.zod.ts:417`, `:601`, the `posture` and `audience` describes drop the noun ("Who may self-register: ...", "who may self-register (...)"). RIGHT, the form PR #24407 gave plugin-auth's two self-registration refusals. Enum, default and optionality unchanged; the JSON-schema description moves, the shape does not; `content/docs/references/system/auth-config.mdx` follows in three rows.
7. `api/protocol.zod.ts:3373`, the `AiModelsResponse.models` describe, "Models this system offers". RIGHT under the second arm, and the spelling #24413 used for the MCP listing warning. The union shape is unchanged. Observation, not a defect: the adjacent `default` describe (`:3371`, "the environment default") and the TSDoc (`:3359`, "the environment's plan-filtered picker list") keep the word, so one shape now carries both nouns; the dev's reason (a deployment's plan-scoped allowlist and its configured default) is sound, and both lines sit outside the card's census.
8. `contracts/metadata-service.ts:393`, a TSDoc example rendering inside `IMetadataService.listDiagnosed`. RIGHT; comment only, no interface member changes. Added to the file surface by the claim amendment 6259830280.
9. Kept with the word, all three RIGHT under the third arm and verified in the cited code: `data/seed-loader.zod.ts:265` and `:269` (`env` is the `prod | dev | test` enum, a deployment tier); `migrations/entries/semantic/18.package-uninstall-environment-wide.ts:21` (the ADR-0131 D6 environment-wide scope as against an organization; the entry's `id` and `acceptanceCriteria` say "environment-wide"); `system/environment-artifact.zod.ts:155` (a per-deployment consent record the control plane writes).
10. Census arithmetic: `git grep "this environment"` over non-test `packages/spec/src` answers 15 at origin/main and 4 at the head, and the 4 are exactly the kept sites. No test in the tree pins any old sentence (a grep over the head tree for each of the seven old sentences finds no test file), and no "created in this system" spelling leaks in.
11. Public surface: no export, authorable key, refusal code, status, issue path or default moves; check:api-surface and check:authorable-surface ran inside the green TypeScript Type Check job. The generated outputs were moved by their generators only and match their sources line for line.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/24406-spec-this-system-copy.md` declares `patch` for `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/platform-objects`. RIGHT. Both manifests at the head carry no `private`, both sit at 18.0.0-next.3, and both ship the moved text (`src/**/*.zod.ts` and `dist` for spec; the generated en bundle for platform-objects). Prose only; no accept set widens or narrows, so patch is the level. `Clause-②: no` sits on the PR body's first lines and in the changeset, with no arm: well-formed and consistent with the diff. The changeset body states FROM and TO for every moved sentence. Check Changeset is green. The `content/docs/references/**` pages are generator-owned and need no declaration of their own.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions`: none declared. Each dev deviation and out-of-scope finding, answered:

- Fence reading (`contracts/metadata-service.ts` changed though the claim listed it by count only): answered. The claim amendment 6259830280 added it to the file surface; no open PR touches it.
- Local build shape (`OS_SKIP_DTS=1`; `check:dts-closure` red locally; `check:skill-examples` and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` not measured): answered by the head's check-runs. TypeScript Type Check, Build Core and Lint and Repo Gates are success on CI's full build.

- Attribution form: the AGENTS.md footer and trailer pair were used. Correct; AGENTS.md outranks the harness reminder.
- `:103` "environment-authored" on the build and register doors, kept: accepted. It is outside the census, and it is the class noun the `packageId` describe itself still uses ("absent = env-authored", unchanged in this PR and in permission.mdx). Noted for the family carrier: the save door and the build door now name the same provenance class with two spellings.
- `api/protocol.zod.ts:3359` cites a bare `ADR-0028`, which this registry resolves to metadata naming: escalated. A pre-existing citation defect outside this card; the seat should file it, or fold it into the family's closing card, spelled `cloud ADR-NNNN` if that is the record meant.
